title: When do we experience effort?
core_idea: The experience of effort is the felt phenomenology that arises when an agent resists affective, behaviour‑guiding signals (e.g. hunger, pain, fatigue, anxiety, temptation). This unified account treats mental and physical effort as cases of resisting such directed, valenced signals and contrasts this approach with cost/opportunity‑cost based explanations.
tldr: The paper sketches an account of the experience of effort as arising from resisting affective behaviour‑guiding signals rather than from signaling costs, aims to unify mental and physical effort, and distinguishes the experience of effort from claims about effort itself.
